Hell Angels hired as security attack a concert goer with pool cues a Rolling Stones concert. Altamont Speedway, California. 1969.

The Altamont Speedway Free Festival was a rock concert for about 300,000 held on Saturday, December 6, 1969, at the Altamont Speedway in northern California. The event is best known for considerable violence. Members of the Hells Angels biker gang had been hired as security in return for $500 of beer.

The concert featured (in order of appearance): Santana, Jefferson Airplane, The Flying Burrito Brothers, and Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young, with the Rolling Stones headlining. The Grateful Dead were scheduled to perform, but declined to play shortly before their scheduled appearance in protest of the Hells Angels knocking out Jefferson Airplane singer Marty Balin while he was performing.

Over the course of the day, the mood of both the crowd and the Angels became progressively agitated and violent. The Angels had been drinking their free beer all day in front of the stage, and most were very drunk. The crowd had also become antagonistic and unpredictable, attacking each other, the Angels and the performers. By the time the Rolling Stones took the stage in the early evening, the mood had taken a decidedly ugly turn as numerous fights had erupted between Angels and crowd members and within the crowd itself.

The violence culminated in the stabbing of Merideth Hunter, who had pulled out a gun after getting into a fight with a Hells Angels member. The Angel was later acquitted of murder on the basis of self-defense.

They are called *nagmists* or, perhaps more often, “the night mists,” a curious weather pattern of unusually thick mists that spring up during the South African night, generally in the more rural areas of the nation. At time, visibility gets reduced to as little as ten feet. The thick mists all but vanish after the first rays of the sun. Many more superstitious group in the nations, such as [Khoisan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khoisan), fear the mist as some sort of supernatural curse upon the nation.

Scientists are not sure why the mist is acting up, but some blame it on something to do with global warming and its effects on South Africa, and thus they urge President Cyril to look into making the nation more green in an effort to keep South Africa safe.
